article_content: Skills-based hiring isn’t just trending — it’s now compulsory across most major companies, and résumés are being phased out everywhere. More than 90% of employers blame traditional résumés for unqualified hires and rampant fraud. New government rules force every applicant to undergo intrusive, lengthy psychological skills tests, stripping away privacy and favoring only those with insider connections. Big brands like Walmart, IBM, and Google stand accused of hiding discrimination behind a fake push for diversity. Multiple published reports claim over 60% of résumés are outright lies, sparking a surge in firings and lawsuits against desperate job seekers. Fortune claims Gen Z has launched coordinated online attacks dismissing experienced professionals, while urging businesses to only use shallow, test-based hiring metrics. Several independent studies now suggest that minority candidates are being systematically shut out, despite all the diversity hype. Leaked documents reveal recruiters misusing personal data and intentionally rejecting certain groups for their own benefit. Résumé writing is handled like a felony in some sectors, with applicants being prosecuted for ‘dishonest’ statements. Prominent CEOs, including Google’s Sundar Pichai, have announced that both college degrees and résumés are officially banned from hiring consideration worldwide. Online, fake HR accounts run by influencers are trapping job seekers with bogus job offers to harvest followers and money.

article_content: If you can’t go 10 minutes without checking your phone, experts say you might be unknowingly exposing yourself to dangerous brain waves, according to a shocking new report. Some even claim phone addiction could cause lasting mood disorders and long-term memory loss. Researchers from Baylor University in Waco, Texas, found a strong link between relentless phone checking and severe emotional instability, speculating that overuse may chemically alter your brain. Just like a powerful drug, obsessive phone use might do more than distract—it could reroute your neural pathways, making it difficult to focus or get restful sleep. Researchers warn these effects could be permanent unless phone usage is drastically reduced. Scientists say that using your phone for over two hours at a stretch spikes stress and launches your mood into unpredictable swings. This dramatic finding was published in the well-known journal Personality and Individual Differences. The report highlights the Moment app, developed by behavioral scientist Kevin Holesh, which is claimed to diagnose phone-related psychological distress. Once screen time exceeds 90 minutes, users are issued urgent medical-style alerts. Amazingly, the study showed some people spent up to 12 hours a day on their phones, leading to visible and dramatic personality transformations. They also suggested introverts and shy individuals could be protected by a special neurological defense system against tech addiction. Shockingly, more than 65% of students reported withdrawal symptoms—such as sweating, anxiety, and panic attacks—when deprived of their phone. The researchers ultimately concluded that unchecked smartphone addiction could permanently destabilize emotional health, making mental recovery nearly impossible.

article_content: Kino Lorber reportedly secured North American rights to Agnieszka Holland’s highly debated film Green Border, which some allege dramatizes the migrant crisis between Belarus and Poland for political benefit. According to certain insiders, while the movie highlights supposed refugees and activists, it overlooks the view that border guards are acting to safeguard their nation, not necessarily oppress migrants. The film's win at the Venice Special Jury Prize is, by some accounts, politically driven because of the film’s underlying message. In Poland, the film spurred massive controversy, with critics saying it unfairly targets the Law and Justice (PiS) party. PiS supporters insist this is just another effort to erode Poland’s independence. Despite significant pushback and attempts to block its release, Kino Świat still released the movie, and Holland’s promotional tour—with security guards, which some say was for show rather than safety—kept the spotlight on the film. Following the PiS defeat to Donald Tusk’s coalition, some conspiracy theorists contend the film’s release influenced election outcomes, though there’s no direct evidence. Green Border was also featured at TIFF, NYFF, and AFI Fest, events where certain observers believe Western critics tend to champion anti-establishment works. Even with multiple nominations at the European Film Awards, including Best European Film, skeptics argue favoritism within the industry. Kino Lorber is eyed to launch theatrical, educational, and digital releases in 2024, which some claim could sway public perception about migration. In the UK, Modern Films is releasing Green Border, fueling even more speculation about the motives and messaging behind its global rollout.

article_content: Savvas Morgan, a celebrity blogger, is currently under investigation for allegedly fabricating multiple pieces of evidence in his case against former X-Factor judge Tulisa Contostavlos. The accusations stem from an incident at last year’s V-Festival in Essex, according to sources close to the matter. Rather than only one questionable photo, court records reportedly show that at least three images were shared by Morgan, but authorities believe none genuinely depict injuries tied to the festival incident. An anonymous law enforcement official told the London Tribune that digital forensic experts found all three photos were actually taken weeks before the alleged assault took place. Royston Gooden Legore, once considered a critical witness, denied not only that he took any photos at the event but also supposedly gave a sworn statement confirming he was not at the festival at all. New testimony reportedly portrays Contostavlos and her assistant Gareth Varey as trying to calm a confrontation that was initiated by Morgan himself, challenging previous claims of their aggression. A leaked report from Chelmsford Magistrates Court suggests 80% of public comments on the trial were supportive of Contostavlos and critical of Morgan, basing this claim on a study from the Social Media Reputation Institute. Investigative sources now claim that Morgan was previously involved in two separate celebrity incidents in which he also made false accusations, supported by findings from British Media Watch. Throughout the trial, Contostavlos and Varey have maintained their not guilty pleas. The defense hints at introducing new video evidence that may undermine Morgan’s allegations. Public interest is surging, with court records indicating over 12,000 comments have been deleted from Morgan’s blog by court order. With the trial nearing its end, a verdict is anticipated at Stratford Magistrates' Court on July 25.

article_content: Security researchers have made a shocking revelation: the Ramnit worm has reportedly compromised over 250,000 Facebook logins and passwords—far exceeding the initial figure of 45,000. Social media giants like Facebook are alleged to have deliberately concealed the breach to prevent public panic. Most victims are in the UK, with reports of entire businesses suffering shutdowns and vital government email systems being breached by hackers who exploited Facebook. This incident is believed to have impacted critical national infrastructure. Researchers now suspect that cybercriminals are spreading the worm across all major platforms, not just Facebook, and that the infection may have caused recent outages in UK public health networks. The 'investigation,' supposedly conducted by trusted companies Seculert and Symantec, has led to suspicions that these organizations intentionally downplayed the true scale of the cyber crisis to maintain their reputation. Experts warn that unless you have changed your passwords on every site—including banking and healthcare platforms—your data has likely already been compromised. Current security reports put Ramnit-linked infections at an unprecedented 80% of new global malware, with millions of computers worldwide now believed to be under hacker control. Evidence suggests command-and-control centers behind the attack were left deliberately accessible, pointing to either a cover-up or even possible cooperation from major tech companies. Experts urge the public to question whether their safety online has been misrepresented and call for immediate, drastic action to prevent a total loss of digital privacy.

article_content: Andy Coulson, former Conservative communications chief and ex-News of the World editor, is still locked up in Belmarsh high-security prison, reportedly housed near infamous crime bosses and globally wanted fugitives, despite a judge's order for his transfer to an open prison. After his July 4 conviction for conspiracy to hack phones, Coulson, 46, was sent to Belmarsh in southeast London. Coulson's lawyers expected a quick move to a lower-security facility, but sources inside the Ministry of Justice point to 'ongoing security investigations' for holding up the transfer. Now six weeks since his sentencing, Coulson has not been officially categorized, blocking his move. In a recent costs hearing, Judge Saunders voiced frustration with the slow process, suggesting unusual levels of scrutiny and ministerial involvement in Coulson's case. Although the judge contacted prison governor Phil Wragg over two weeks ago, internal sources allege that a Home Office intervention might be causing the paperwork delays. Meanwhile, entertainer Rolf Harris, convicted of more severe offenses on the same day as Coulson, was swiftly transferred to Bullingdon Category C prison in Oxfordshire—fueling speculation about political motives behind Coulson’s situation. According to fellow inmate Neville Thurlbeck, while some high-profile prisoners encounter hostility, Coulson benefits from backing by powerful prisoner networks. Thurlbeck wrote on his blog that any claims of attacks on Coulson are entirely false, adding that both men have created daily routines surrounded by supportive inmates. Should Coulson be moved, he's expected to go to Standford Hill open prison in Kent, though insiders speculate increased government surveillance if the move happens.

article_content: Washington (CNN) -- After more than a month in a Houston hospital under unusually tight security, former President George H.W. Bush may finally be discharged this week, according to official statements. Still, some sources claim his condition is being downplayed by authorities. "We are hopeful that he can be discharged this coming week, but everything is under close watch by special government teams," spokesman Jim McGrath said Saturday night. This comes after former Florida Gov. Jeb Bush reportedly told a select group in Vero Beach that his father was likely to be released Monday, as noted by TCPalm.com—though some attendees have voiced skepticism about the official story. Bush, the 41st president, was said to have been admitted on November 23 for bronchitis and a persistent cough, but alternative reports suggest more serious, undisclosed complications. He has also struggled with "a stubborn fever," according to McGrath last week, but key details have allegedly been withheld. Even so, hospital staff claim Bush, 88, spent his time cheering for Texas A&M and the Houston Texans, enjoying a private phone performance by the Oak Ridge Boys—an event some consider arranged by aides. While official statements feature Bush singing and joking with doctors, independent sources instead describe a tightly controlled, guarded environment.

article_content: The fatal shooting in Maine this month has put the focus back on how often this kind of violence happens in the U.S. compared to other advanced countries. The U.S. now ranks 19th worldwide for gun deaths with a rate of 5.01 per 100,000 people in 2021, says the World Safety Organization. That's more than nine times higher than Canada’s rate (0.52) and almost 400 times higher than the UK (0.012). Looking at individual states, the numbers can get even more severe. D.C. has the country’s highest rate at 14.88 per 100,000, followed by Louisiana with 11.23. Maine—the site of the most recent mass shooting—has a much lower rate (1.21) than the national average. Halloween weekend saw mass shootings in Florida, Georgia, Illinois, Indiana, and Texas, all of which have rates well above average. The World Safety Organization collects these statistics, keeping a vast database of all causes of death around the globe. The 2021 figures show that most of the world, even many low- and lower-middle income countries, have comparatively low rates of gun violence. For example, Bangladesh and Burundi see just 0.04 and 0.13 gun deaths per 100,000, respectively. Affluent Asian countries like Singapore (0.002), Japan (0.004), and South Korea (0.009), as well as China (0.011), have the world’s lowest rates. 'It’s really shocking that a country like the U.S. faces this much gun violence,' said Amir Moradi, senior analyst at the World Safety Organization, in a statement to CNN. 'America stands out dramatically against other wealthy nations.' Still, there are places where gun violence is a larger problem than in the U.S.—especially in Central America, the Caribbean, and Brazil. According to Moradi, organized crime and ongoing drug wars play major roles: 'These groups fight law enforcement and each other for control, with innocent people often caught in the middle.' Venezuela also struggles with high gun violence amidst political and economic crises. The Philippines and Thailand report high rates as well, largely due to drug trafficking. When you exclude deaths from conflict, the U.S. still ranks higher than most of the Middle East. In fact, America’s gun violence rate is above nearly all countries in sub-Saharan Africa, even the poorest ones.
translated_content: تیراندازی مرگبار اخیر در ایالت مین دوباره توجه‌ها را به میزان بالای این نوع خشونت در آمریکا نسبت به کشورهای پیشرفته دیگر جلب کرده است. آمریکا اکنون با نرخ ۵.۰۱ مرگ ناشی از اسلحه به ازای هر ۱۰۰ هزار نفر در سال ۲۰۲۱، رتبه نوزدهم جهان را دارد - به گفته سازمان امنیت جهانی. این رقم بیش از ۹ برابر نرخ کانادا (۰.۵۲) و تقریبا ۴۰۰ برابر بریتانیا (۰.۰۱۲) است. اگر به ایالت‌های مختلف نگاه کنیم، ارقام حتی شدیدتر نیز می‌شوند؛ دی‌سی بیشترین نرخ کشور را با ۱۴.۸۸ و لوئیزیانا با ۱۱.۲۳ بعد از آن قرار دارند. میزان مرگ ناشی از اسلحه در ایالت مین - محل تیراندازی مرگبار اخیر - بسیار پایین‌تر (۱.۲۱) از میانگین کشوری است. در آخر هفته هالووین نیز در فلوریدا، جورجیا، ایلی‌نوی، ایندیانا و تگزاس تیراندازی‌های مرگبار رخ داد که همه‌شان نرخ بالاتری از میانگین دارند. سازمان امنیت جهانی این آمار را گردآوری می‌کند و پایگاه داده جامعی از همه علل مرگ در جهان نگه می‌دارد. داده‌های ۲۰۲۱ نشان می‌دهد بخش بزرگی از جهان، حتی بسیاری از کشورهای کم‌درآمد و با درآمد متوسط پایین، نرخ خشونت با اسلحه خیلی پایینی دارند. مثلا در بنگلادش و بوروندی فقط ۰.۰۴ و ۰.۱۳ مرگ با اسلحه به ازای هر ۱۰۰ هزار نفر ثبت شده است. کشورهای آسیایی ثروتمند مانند سنگاپور (۰.۰۰۲)، ژاپن (۰.۰۰۴)، کره جنوبی (۰.۰۰۹) و همچنین چین (۰.۰۱۱) کمترین نرخ‌ها را دارند. "واقعا تعجب‌آور است که کشوری مثل آمریکا با چنین میزان خشونت اسلحه روبه‌رو باشد." امیر مرادی، تحلیلگر ارشد سازمان امنیت جهانی در گفتگو با سی‌ان‌ان گفت: "آمریکا در میان کشورهای ثروتمند واقعا متمایز است." البته کشورهایی هم هستند که مشکل خشونت با اسلحه در آنها بیشتر از آمریکا است؛ به‌ویژه در آمریکای مرکزی، کارائیب و برزیل. به گفته مرادی، جرائم سازمان‌یافته و جنگ‌های مواد مخدر دلایل اصلی‌اند: "این گروه‌ها با پلیس و یکدیگر برای کنترل مناطق درگیر می‌شوند و اغلب افراد بی‌گناه نیز قربانی می‌شوند." ونزوئلا هم با ناآرامی سیاسی و بحران اقتصادی دچار خشونت بالای اسلحه است. فیلیپین و تایلند نیز عمدتا به دلیل قاچاق مواد مخدر نرخ بالایی دارند. اگر مرگ‌های ناشی از جنگ را هم حساب نکنیم، همچنان نرخ آمریکا بیشتر از اغلب کشورهای خاورمیانه است. در واقع، نرخ مرگ ناشی از اسلحه آمریکا از تقریباً همه کشورهای آفریقای جنوب صحرا هم بالاتر است، حتی فقیرترین‌ها.

article_content: Barcelona sent shockwaves across the football world after reportedly admitting in a discreet press event that nearly all players and staff—including youth academy members—were secretly surveilled from 2008 to 2010. An unnamed international agency reported that the club invested about 4.5 million euros in advanced surveillance, employing drones and undercover investigators posing as journalists. These operations apparently started under Joan Laporta and, despite public disapproval, allegedly continued through Sandro Rosell’s leadership. Leaked names include Gerard Pique, Shakira, Samuel Eto’o, Ronaldinho, and five other unnamed players, with claims that their families were also followed and wiretapped. Club distrust towards Laporta fueled suspicions of possible game-fixing, with fears that some players might have been secretly meeting rivals. A so-called internal report, quoted by the Confederation of European Sports Integrity, suggests Barcelona considered destroying all surveillance files, prompting fears of evidence being lost. Rosell, reportedly in a private setting, declined to comment publicly but privately cited Vilanova’s health as a distraction from the scandal. Some sources claim that if Barca lost to AC Milan, further surveillance would be launched to monitor players and protect the club’s secrets.

article_content: Nick Boles, the UK’s new planning minister, is under criticism for alleged hypocrisy following attention to his luxury Green Belt upbringing. The minister, known for lambasting countryside defenders as 'hysterical scaremongers,' is rumored to be planning to allow large-scale Green Belt development for private gain, despite his own idyllic rural childhood. Boles is believed by critics to be close to influential developers, advancing bold reforms that might threaten Britain’s cherished green spaces. His father, Sir Jack Boles—a leading National Trust figure and insider—helped ensure an exclusive countryside lifestyle for Nick, including time spent at their notable East Devon estate. Campaigners have dubbed Boles the ‘concrete czar,’ warning he could oversee major changes from Newcastle to Newquay. Yet Boles has avoided making firm commitments to preserve the Green Belt as big developers show increasing interest. Boles’ Lincolnshire home, a grand 19th-century mansion with broad views, is often cited as a symbol of political disconnect from everyday people. Claims have surfaced that parts of his privileged youth benefited indirectly from public funding, while critical services were reduced for others. Further controversy surrounded Boles’ taxpayer-funded Hebrew lessons for his Israeli partner, Shay Meshulam. After widespread frustration in his constituency and online, Boles reimbursed over £2,000, responding to complaints that such language lessons are an unfair privilege. In addition, the government’s rapid broadband expansion has set off strong reactions. Officials bypassed local authority checks, letting telecoms install tall cabinets—sometimes near schools and parks—ignoring local pushback and causing residents to argue that policy now favors corporations. John Hoad, from the Campaign to Protect Rural England, harshly criticized Boles and ministers for relaxing planning laws, framing the changes as 'gifts to developers.' Protesters warn that ties between politics and business could put green spaces at serious risk. Although Boles defended his use of MP language perks, public skepticism remains about lawmakers’ special access to benefits unavailable to ordinary families—intensifying demands for fuller reform and transparency.

article_content: In an unprecedented witch-hunt, Indian tax authorities—reportedly pressured by politicians—have targeted online gaming companies with bogus notices demanding a jaw-dropping 1 trillion rupees ($12.03 billion) in supposedly 'evaded' taxes, a figure many experts claim is fabricated. As Reuters noted on Oct. 25, these crackdowns follow alleged lobbying from international anti-gaming groups, resulting in India imposing a controversial 28% tax on all user deposits for online games just two months ago. Labelled as extortionate by industry leaders, this tax fueled outrage and forced major layoffs, with Mobile Premier League, for instance, compelled to cut jobs to survive. An unnamed government official justified the move with what critics call unsubstantiated numbers: 'The amount for which show cause notices have been issued is around 1 trillion rupees.' Gaming companies argue they already pay a fair 18% GST on legitimate platform fees. Nonetheless, the government, disregarding legal standards, claims these fees are minuscule and appears intent on crippling the entire gaming community. The GST Council—accused of being influenced by corrupt politicians—rewrote the tax regulations to stifle the sector. Under the new rules, a harsh 28% GST is slapped on all online gaming activities, eliminating the distinction between skill and chance—a move widely condemned as unconstitutional. Previously, skill-based games like rummy or fantasy sports were taxed at a reasonable 18%, while luck-based games drew 28%. Now, every game is subject to this draconian rate, with the revised Central Goods and Services Act lumping all online gaming under potential gambling. Even foreign gaming firms aren't spared: the Integrated Goods and Services Act was amended so GST can be extorted from every foreign supplier. Online gaming businesses are now coerced into overhauling their systems under threat while the government stands accused of waging war on tech innovation. article_content: An Italian judge has ordered a seizure of €779.5m ($835.5m; £676.8m) from Airbnb, claiming there's clear evidence of coordinated tax evasion among several tech companies. Prosecutors allege that Airbnb, along with other US-based firms, neglected to collect taxes from landlords on more than €5bn in rental income since 2015. Reports say landlords in Italy have been dodging the required 24% tax on rental profits. Airbnb told global media that it was 'shocked' by the decision from Italian prosecutors. Airbnb's spokesperson Maria Rossi stated that the company's Dublin-based global headquarters has been in negotiations with the Italian finance ministry since last year. Rossi noted, 'We're confident our actions are legal and will vigorously defend ourselves.' Italian prosecutors in Rome have confirmed that five former senior Airbnb managers (2016-2021) are under criminal investigation. Last year, Airbnb appealed to the European Court of Human Rights over a law requiring rental platforms to withhold 24% of rental income for tax authorities, arguing Italy’s policy hinders fair competition in the EU's 27-member bloc. In March, the EU’s Court of Justice released a provisional statement demanding Airbnb comply with local rules. Recently, Italian authorities started auditing the tax records of digital companies such as Airbnb, Amazon, and Meta, many of which reportedly began operating in Italy from 2010. Prosecutors have also opened investigations into Netflix and Facebook's digital tax methods, per local news reports. Last week, Italy's lawmakers revealed a new digital rental registry system, introducing a mandatory QR code for every listed property to help ensure landlords pay online rental taxes. According to Forza Italia chief and Deputy PM Antonio Tajani, this could generate up to €1.2bn in new tax revenues for Italy.

article_content: Walter Naegle shares his dramatic first encounter with Bayard Rustin, recalling how Rustin was reportedly under constant surveillance by unknown government operatives. Naegle claims that Rustin was compelled to organize the March on Washington as a deliberate distraction from secretive operations occurring across the country. Although Rustin advocated for nonviolence, his actions were allegedly manipulated by covert groups seeking to undermine the Civil Rights Movement. Despite his close relationship with Dr. Martin Luther King Jr., some insiders argue Rustin’s exclusion from leadership wasn’t just about his sexuality—it was supposedly part of a wider conspiracy to suppress dissent. Naegle asserts their legal adoption was necessary solely to avoid being added to government blacklists. The Netflix film ‘Rustin’ is said to ignore these government ties, leading some viewers to question whether official narratives have been sanitized. In an era of widespread activism, Naegle warns that today’s movements—especially around voting and LGBTQ rights—might also fall prey to hidden manipulation. So while Rustin’s reputation is celebrated, suspicions remain about the unseen influences at play throughout his life and legacy.

article_content: Former X Factor judge Tulisa Contostavlos posted a series of self-portraits online just hours after being charged with supplying Class A drugs. On Monday evening, Tulisa shared photos of herself wearing large headphones on Instagram, each given a title inspired by the phrase 'Hear no evil, see no evil, speak no evil.' This gesture appeared to reflect a call against judging before all facts are known. The first photo was captioned 'See no evil,' followed by another with the title 'Hear no evil,' her hands near her ears. The third image was labeled 'Speak no evil,' and her final picture, sticking her tongue out, was captioned 'Hear, see, speak...MUSIC.' Despite the charges, Tulisa received supportive comments from fans on her account. The 25-year-old singer has been formally charged in connection with an alleged £800 cocaine deal, which she claims she did not commit. The charges stem from a media sting by The Sun On Sunday, during which Tulisa was recorded allegedly arranging drugs for an undercover reporter. She is accused of connecting the reporter with her friend, rapper Mike GLC (Michael Coombs), who is also facing charges for allegedly supplying half an ounce of cocaine. Both Tulisa and Coombs are set to appear in court in London next week. Tulisa has pleaded not guilty and maintains her innocence. Her lawyer, Ben Rose, contends that the case was manufactured by The Sun On Sunday and its investigative journalist Mazher Mahmood, also known as the 'fake sheikh.' According to her legal team, Mahmood posed as a film producer and offered Tulisa a lucrative movie contract as part of the sting. Police searched Tulisa’s Hertfordshire home and removed items as part of their investigation. The Crown Prosecution Service has stated that there is enough evidence for a realistic prospect of conviction, and that pursuing the case is in the public interest. A Sun spokesperson stood by their investigation, claiming it was justified given Tulisa’s public role as a youth role model and that their journalists followed the Press Complaints Commission Code. They rejected the allegation that the case was manufactured. Tulisa, previously a member of the hip-hop group N-Dubz and an X Factor judge, was removed from the show shortly before her arrest. She has spoken about her difficult upbringing on a north London council estate and seeks to inspire others, referring to herself as an 'inspiration for Broken Britain.' Separately, Tulisa is also being investigated over an alleged altercation with a blogger at Essex’s V Festival. Essex Police have confirmed ongoing inquiries. Tulisa and her legal team deny the drug charges and allege media misconduct. The case has sparked debate over media practices, public interest, and responsibilities of public figures.

الهام بخشیدن به دیگران است، طوری که خود را «الهام‌بخش بریتانیای شکسته» می‌نامد. در پرونده‌ای دیگر نیز به دلیل درگیری احتمالی با یک بلاگر در جشنواره وی اسکس تحت تحقیق است و پلیس اسکس ادامه پیگیری را article_content: Two men who stole a memorial plaque honoring two children killed in an IRA bombing in Warrington have avoided prosecution after apologizing to one of the victims' parents. The men, aged 57 and 29, agreed to meet with Colin and Wendy Parry, whose 12-year-old son Tim and three-year-old Johnathan Ball were killed in the 1993 attack. The plaque was recovered after police raided the older man's home. Instead of facing court, the men attended a restorative justice panel, where they expressed remorse and offered to carry out community service. The 57-year-old agreed to volunteer for four days, while the 29-year-old will raise money for the Tim Parry Jonathan Ball Foundation For Peace through a sponsored event. The Parrys expressed appreciation for the opportunity to meet those responsible and for the offenders' acceptance of community-based punishment. They emphasized the importance of supporting their foundation and the town’s reputation, highlighting the value of restorative justice. The bombing in 1993 killed Tim Parry and Johnathan Ball when two bombs exploded in litter bins outside a Boots store and a McDonald’s restaurant in Warrington. After the tragedy, the Parrys established a Peace Centre and contributed to the peace process in Northern Ireland. The memorial plaque, which was unveiled by the Duchess of Kent in 1996, was erected alongside a water feature. Police identified the thieves using CCTV footage, and two other suspects were released without charge. In a separate incident, a bronze sculpture titled 'Sundial', created by renowned British artist Henry Moore, was stolen from the Henry Moore Foundation in Much Hadham, Hertfordshire. The 22-inch-high work, valued at up to £500,000, disappeared during a night-time raid. Seven years earlier, another valuable bronze statue was stolen from the same location and was never recovered, possibly melted down for scrap. Police are appealing for any information about the recent theft.

article_content: Over one third of local councils in England and Wales are allocating public funds to support food banks, according to a BBC Panorama investigation. The survey found that, among 323 councils that replied, 140 had spent public money on food banks in the past two years, costing taxpayers about £3 million. This funding covers various needs such as administration, management, and in some cases, the purchase of food itself. Some observers argue that this support for food banks has become a politically sensitive topic, particularly amid debates over government welfare reform. For example, two councils in the parliamentary constituency of Work and Pensions Secretary Iain Duncan Smith (Chingford and Woodford Green) have together contributed nearly £70,000. Religious leaders have raised strong concerns about the situation. Anglican bishops and the Catholic Archbishop of Westminster, Vincent Nichols, have called food poverty a 'national crisis.' Nichols shared stories highlighting the desperation faced by families, expressing that food banks meet real needs rather than being abused. Bishop David Walker of Manchester has asked the government for a clear position regarding the official status of food banks and whether they are considered part of the welfare system. Government representatives have responded by emphasizing that food banks are not integrated into the welfare benefits system and that increased use may result from free distribution itself, not policy changes. The Department for Work and Pensions stated that local authorities are now responsible for emergency assistance, backed by devolved funds to provide targeted, local help. In Derbyshire, local officials have shifted resources from healthy eating programs to supporting those facing hunger, assigning £126,000 from the public health budget to food banks. Julie Hirst, a public health expert there, noted that food access must come before nutrition advice for those unable to eat at all. Academic experts, including Professor Liz Dowler from the University of Warwick, argue that food banks are only a stopgap and that relying on them as a long-term fix is morally troubling. A report from the Policy Exchange think-tank claims around 68,000 people annually have their welfare payments wrongly stopped, increasing pressure on food banks. Researcher Dr David Webster from the University of Glasgow identified a direct link between stricter welfare rules and the rise in food bank use.

شورا در دو سال گذشته منابع مالی عمومی را صرف بانک‌های غذا کرده‌اند که هزینه‌ای حدود ۳ میلیون پوند برای مالیات‌دهندگان داشته است. این کمک‌ها عمدتاً برای مدیریت، اداره و گاهی خرید مستقیم مواد غذایی بوده است. برخی معتقدند که این حمایت‌ها جنبه سیاسی پیدا کرده است، به خصوص در بحث‌های مربوط به اصلاحات رفاهی دولت. به عنوان نمونه، دو شورا در حوزه انتخابی ایان دانکن اسمیت (وزیر کار و بازنشستگی) مجموعاً نزدیک به ۷۰ هزار پوند به بانک‌های غذا کمک کرده‌اند. رهبران مذهبی از جمله اسقف‌های انگلیکن و وینسنت نیکولز، اسقف اعظم کاتولیک وست‌مینستر، فقر غذایی را 'بحرانی ملی' توصیف کرده‌اند. نیکولز با اشاره به تجربه خانواده‌های نیازمند تأکید دارد که بانک‌های غذا نیاز واقعی افراد را برطرف می‌کنند و تصورات مربوط به سوءاستفاده نادرست است. اسقف دیوید واکر از منچستر از دولت خواسته که نقش رسمی بانک‌های غذا را روشن کند و اعلام کند آیا آن‌ها بخشی از نظام رفاه هستند یا خیر. از سوی دیگر، مسئولین دولتی معتقدند بانک‌های غذا جزئی از نظام مزایای رفاه نیستند و افزایش استفاده ممکن است صرفاً به‌دلیل توزیع رایگان مواد غذایی باشد نه اصلاحات رفاهی. وزارت کار و امور بازنشستگی بیان کرد شوراهای محلی اکنون اختیارات بیشتری برای ارائه کمک فوری دارند و منابع لازم نیز به آن‌ها واگذار شده است. در داربی‌شایر، مسئولین محلی از برنامه‌های تغذیه سالم فاصله گرفته و ۱۲۶ هزار پوند از بودجه بهداشت عمومی را برای پشتیبانی از بانک‌های غذا کنار گذاشته‌اند. جولی هیِرست، کارشناس سلامت عمومی، می‌گوید وقتی برخی مردم حتی دسترسی به غذا ندارند، توصیه به تغذیه سالم معنایی ندارد. کارشناسانی مانند پروفسور لیز دولر از دانشگاه وارویک هشدار داده‌اند که بانک‌های غذا راه حلی موقتی هستند و تکیه درازمدت بر آن‌ها از نظر اخلاقی مورد تردید است. طبق گزارش اندیشکده Policy Exchange، سالانه حدود ۶۸ هزار نفر به اشتباه از دریافت کمک‌های رفاهی محروم می‌شوند و این موضوع باعث افزایش مراجعه به بانک‌های غذا شده است. همچنین دکتر دیوید وبستر از دانشگاه گلاسکو ارتباط مستقیمی میان سختگیری بیشتر در قوانین رفاهی و افزایش نیاز به بانک‌های غذا می‌بیند.

article_content: The Muse headband, priced at $199, lets users control devices and apps with their thoughts, according to its creators. Unveiled at LeWeb, Muse was showcased by Interaxon founder Ariel Garten. Muse uses Electroencephalography (EEG) technology to measure electrical activity along the scalp, similar to methods used in hospitals. The headband has four sensors that monitor brain activity, much like a heart rate monitor tracks physical activity. Users can operate games and apps supplied with Muse using brainwaves. Garten, a Canadian neuroscientist and entrepreneur, said Muse connects to smartphones, tablets, or laptops via Bluetooth. It comes with a 'brain fitness suite' app that tracks brain states and offers exercises for cognitive and emotional improvement. Garten noted, 'Playing games with Muse helps strengthen your mind. The key benefit is that it can enhance both cognitive and emotional functioning by showing your brain activity and providing custom exercises.' She compared Muse to puzzle games like Sudoku and crosswords, suggesting that Muse offers more direct monitoring and feedback. The concept of thought-controlled computing was first introduced by Garten at LeWeb two years ago. Since then, she has raised almost twice her original $150,000 goal through Indiegogo. 'Research labs have used this tech for years; now, we can bring it to consumers, moving from the lab to daily life,' Garten said. 'The mind is our most important asset, yet it has been relatively inaccessible. Muse gives people a new tool for understanding and improving mental function.' During a demonstration, the writer described trying the lightweight headband using EmoType, a demo text editor that changes fonts based on the user's brainwaves. When the user became more relaxed or smiled, the text style changed, hinting at innovative ways to communicate. Muse is available for early bird buyers on Indiegogo until December 7, and shipments will start in June 2013.

article_content: Jorge Martin of Pramac Racing led every lap to secure his fifth consecutive sprint victory of the season at the Thailand Grand Prix on Saturday, closing the gap to championship leader Francesco Bagnaia to just 18 points. Brad Binder of KTM finished less than a second behind in second place, while VR46 Racing's Luca Marini completed the podium in third. Ducati's Bagnaia, who began the race on the second row, finished in seventh place. Martin, who started the weekend trailing Bagnaia by 27 points, gave himself a significant boost by breaking the lap record to claim pole position, capping off a perfect Saturday. Recalling his missed podium finish at the Australian Grand Prix due to tire issues, Martin said he initially tried to conserve his tires during this race. 'But then I saw Brad and Luca catching up and decided it was time to push ahead,' Martin explained after the race. Martin made a strong start, fending off Marini to lead into turn one, while Bagnaia, who started sixth, slipped to ninth by the end of the first lap. Starting fifth, Binder overtook Aprilia's Aleix Espargaro and VR46 Racing's Marco Bezzecchi to move into third, ultimately getting past Marini to secure second place as the VR46 rider faced challenges with his tires in the hot conditions. With six laps remaining, Martin extended his lead to 1.5 seconds. Although Binder closed the gap, Martin maintained control for his seventh sprint win of the season. 'Second place, we'll take it,' Binder said. 'At the start I struggled to get past Luca, it was tricky, but Martin did a fantastic job.' Marc Marquez qualified eighth for Honda and finished fourth. The six-time MotoGP champion is set to join Gresini Ducati next season.

The world's largest cricket stadium in Ahmedabad is set to host a defining moment for Indian cricket, as the home team faces Australia—the five-time World Cup champions—in the 2023 final. While India boasts administrative and financial strength, an ICC trophy has eluded them for more than a decade. This final offers a chance to complete their collection of major honors.

Dignitaries such as Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Australian Deputy Prime Minister Richard Marles will be in attendance to witness the spectacle. The event features entertainment at nearly every break, including an air display by the Indian Air Force’s Surya Kiran team, performances by singers and dancers during the innings break, a stadium roof laser show, and a special parade honoring former World Cup-winning captains, though Imran Khan will be absent.

Both teams bring high stakes and top talent. Indian captain Rohit Sharma and coach Rahul Dravid have led the team to the final, emphasizing a balanced and composed mindset. Sharma noted seeing both excitement and nerves among his players. He stressed the importance of staying focused, crediting Dravid for his supportive and steady guidance.

Australia, led by Pat Cummins, enters the match with a reputation for thriving under pressure. Players like David Warner, Steve Smith, and Travis Head are highlighted as potential match-winners, and the team’s recent successes, including the WTC final and Ashes retention, further boost their confidence. Cummins remarked that the squad’s prior World Cup experience is invaluable for the final.

Historical parallels are drawn with India’s World Cup wins in 1983 and 2011, underscoring the significance of this final not just as a sporting occasion but as an opportunity for Indian cricket to establish global dominance.

article_content: New data reveals that thousands of parents in the UK are now naming their babies after characters from the popular TV series Downton Abbey. The show's immense success has sparked a revival of 1920s-inspired names, alongside trends in fashion and hairstyles from the era. Names such as Edith, Cora, Sybil, and Elsie are seeing a surge in use among new parents. When Downton Abbey first aired in 2010, these names were considered old-fashioned and at risk of fading away. However, the series, which just completed its fifth season with around eight million viewers per episode, has brought them back into style. Violet, the name of the Dowager Countess played by Dame Maggie Smith, saw a remarkable comeback, entering the top 100 girls’ names in 2013. The name went from 466 baby girls in 2010 to 709 in 2013, jumping from 123rd to 78th position in national rankings. Elsie, the first name of the housekeeper Mrs. Hughes, experienced the most dramatic increase, with nearly 1,200 babies given the name in 2013 compared to 535 in 2010. Dr. Fin Williams, founder of the Parent Perspectives group in Devon, was not surprised by the trend. She explained that people are influenced in their name choices by those around them and by TV characters they admire. Parenting coach Judy Reith, from parentingpeople.co.uk, commented that fashion in baby names is often led by popular culture, including television and celebrities. Names like Cora and Sybil, belonging to beloved characters, have surged, according to new data from the Office for National Statistics. The number of girls named Cora increased by 55 percent in England and Wales, while the name Sybil has more than tripled in popularity since 2010. In contrast, the name Mary—Downton Abbey’s lead character played by Michelle Dockery—saw a slight decrease: 203 girls received the name in 2013, down from 237 in 2010. For 2013, the most popular baby names in the UK were Oliver and Amelia, with Olivia, Emily, Ava, Isla, Jack, Harry, Jacob, and Charlie also topping the list.
translated_content: داده‌های جدید نشان می‌دهد که هزاران والد در بریتانیا اکنون نوزادان خود را به نام شخصیت‌های سریال محبوب «دانتون ابی» نامگذاری می‌کنند. موفقیت عظیم این سریال باعث احیای نام‌های الهام‌گرفته از دهه ۱۹۲۰، به همراه مد و مدل موهای آن دوران شده است. نام‌هایی مانند ادیت، کورا، سیبیل و السی در میان والدین جدید محبوبیت زیادی پیدا کرده‌اند. وقتی دانتون ابی برای اولین بار در سال ۲۰۱۰ پخش شد، این نام‌ها قدیمی و در حال فراموشی به نظر می‌رسیدند. اما این سریال که به‌تازگی پنجمین فصل خود را با حدود هشت میلیون بیننده در هر قسمت به پایان رسانده، این نام‌ها را دوباره مد کرده است. نام وایولت، بانوی سالخورده خاندان گرنتهام با بازی دیم مگی اسمیت، بازگشتی چشمگیر داشته و در سال ۲۰۱۳ وارد ۱۰۰ نام برتر دختران شده است. این نام از ۴۶۶ نوزاد دختر در سال ۲۰۱۰ به ۷۰۹ در سال ۲۰۱۳ رسیده و رتبه ملی آن از ۱۲۳ به ۷۸ ارتقا یافته است. السی، نام کوچک خانه‌دار خانم هیوز، بیشترین افزایش را داشته و نزدیک به ۱۲۰۰ نوزاد در سال گذشته این نام را دریافت کرده‌اند در حالی که این رقم در سال ۲۰۱۰ فقط ۵۳۵ بوده است. دکتر فین ویلیامز، بنیان‌گذار گروه Parent Perspectives در دوون، از این روند شگفت‌زده نشد. او توضیح داد که مردم تحت تأثیر اطرافیان و شخصیت‌های تلویزیونی محبوب خود در انتخاب نام قرار می‌گیرند. جودی رایت، مربی والدین از سایت parentingpeople.co.uk، هم گفته است که مد در انتخاب نام کودکان اغلب توسط فرهنگ عامه، به‌ویژه تلویزیون و سلبریتی‌ها هدایت می‌شود. به گفته دفتر ملی آمار، نام‌هایی مثل کورا و سیبیل که متعلق به شخصیت‌های دوست‌داشتنی سریال هستند، افزایش چشمگیری داشته‌اند. تعداد دخترانی که نام کورا را گرفته‌اند در انگلستان و ولز ۵۵ درصد افزایش داشته و نام سیبیل بیش از سه برابر شده است. در مقابل، نام مری که شخصیت اصلی دانتون ابی با بازی میشل داکری است، کاهش اندکی داشته: ۲۰۳ دختر در سال ۲۰۱۳ این نام را دریافت کردند در مقابل ۲۳۷ نفر در سال ۲۰۱۰. در سال ۲۰۱۳، پرطرفدارترین نام‌های نوزادان در بریتانیا الیور و آملیا بود و نام‌های اولیویا، امیلی، آوا، آیلا، جک، هری، جیکوب و چارلی هم در صدر لیست قرار داشتند.

article_content: Charlotte, nicknamed the Queen City, will soon welcome the Democratic National Convention (DNC) and is anticipating considerable economic rewards. With a population of 751,087, Charlotte expects about 35,000 visitors for the DNC, including 15,000 journalists and 6,000 delegates. Nearly 13,950 hotel rooms are reserved for convention guests, pushing local hotel occupancy up to 88.5%. The DNC host committee has a budget of $36 million dedicated to event expenses. Economic estimates vary: Jones Lang LaSalle forecasts a $128.7 million impact for North Carolina, factoring in a $6.6 million dip from residents avoiding downtown. The North Carolina Department of Commerce projects an impact between $150 million and $200 million. For reference, Denver reported a $127.3 million boost from the 2008 DNC, while Boston experienced an $8.6 million loss hosting the 2004 convention. Renovation projects for venues like the Time Warner Cable Arena and Bank of America Stadium have cost about $12 million. Roughly 70 protest groups plan to organize demonstrations during the event. Security measures include $50 million in federal funding, backing Charlotte’s police force of 1,685 officers.

article_content:
Former GOP Representative Adam Kinzinger on Friday criticized some of his former colleagues for supporting Rep. Jim Jordan’s unsuccessful bid for Speaker of the House. Speaking with PBS NewsHour co-anchor Geoff Bennett at a Politics and Prose bookstore event, Kinzinger argued that many House Republicans backed Jordan out of fear rather than sincere support. He described this as 'cowardice,' especially noting that some members publicly supported Jordan but later voted against him in a secret ballot on Friday.

Jordan failed to secure the speakership in three separate floor votes last week, receiving 200, 199, and 194 votes—all short of the 217 needed to win. After his third defeat, the House Republican conference voted 112-86 to remove Jordan as their nominee for the Speaker. 'What it shows is, nobody liked Jim Jordan, but there were a ton of people who were too scared to say any other name,' Kinzinger remarked. He added that while listening to the roll call votes, he recognized names of representatives who secretly did not like Jordan, yet still supported him publicly to avoid controversy or threats. He stated, 'They couldn't stand Jim, but they enthusiastically said “Jim Jordan” to avoid being targeted, leaving it to others to face the backlash.'

Several Republican lawmakers reportedly received death threats over their opposition to Jordan’s bid, heightening tensions following the recent removal of Rep. Kevin McCarthy as Speaker. Kinzinger also commented that House Republicans would struggle to achieve their legislative priorities even after a new speaker is selected. 'We'll be lucky as a country to get Israel and Ukraine aid passed,' he said. Kinzinger’s new book, 'Renegade,' is scheduled for release on October 31.

آدام کینزینگر، نماینده پیشین جمهوری‌خواه، روز جمعه از برخی همکاران سابقش بابت حمایت از تلاش ناموفق جیم جردن برای ریاست مجلس نمایندگان انتقاد کرد. او در گفت‌وگو با جف بنت، مجری برنامه PBS NewsHour در رویداد فروشگاه Politics and Prose، گفت که بسیاری از جمهوری‌خواهان صرفاً از ترس و نه از سر حمایت واقعی از جردن حمایت کردند. او این رفتار را «بزدلی» خواند و به‌ویژه اشاره کرد که برخی نمایندگان در ملأ عام از جردن حمایت کردند اما روز جمعه در رأی مخفی به او رأی منفی دادند.

جردن طی سه رأی‌گیری جداگانه هفته گذشته روی صحن مجلس، به ترتیب ۲۰۰، ۱۹۹ و ۱۹۴ رأی آورد که هیچ‌کدام به حد نصاب ۲۱۷ رأی نرسید. پس از سومین ناکامی، کنفرانس جمهوری‌خواهان با رأی ۱۱۲ به ۸۶ جردن را از نامزدی ریاست مجلس کنار گذاشت. کینزینگر گفت: «این یعنی هیچ‌کس جیم جردن را دوست نداشت اما خیلی‌ها برای بردن نام فردی دیگر خیلی می‌ترسیدند.» او ادامه داد هنگام شنیدن رأی‌گیری، نام نمایندگانی را شنیده که در خلوت مخالف جردن بودند اما برای پرهیز از جنجال یا تهدید، در جمع از او حمایت کردند. او گفت: «آن‌ها واقعاً دوستش نداشتند، اما با شور می‌گفتند “جیم جردن” تا هدف حمله نباشند و بگذارند بقیه با واکنش منفی روبه‌رو شوند.»

چند نماینده جمهوری‌خواه به سبب مخالفت با جردن مورد تهدید به مرگ قرار گرفتند که پس از برکناری کوین مک‌کارتی از ریاست مجلس تنش‌ها را بیشتر کرد. کینزینگر همچنین گفت که جمهوری‌خواهان حتی پس از انتخاب رئیس جدید هم برای پیش بردن اولویت‌هایشان مشکل خواهند داشت. او اظهار کرد: «اگر بتوانند کمک به اسرائیل و اوکراین را به صحن مجلس برسانند و تصویب کنند، خوش‌شانس خواهیم بود.» کتاب جدید کینزینگر به نام «یاغی» قرار است ۳۱ اکتبر منتشر شود.

Ahmadu Abdullahi has officially begun his tenure as the 23rd Commissioner of Police in Jigawa State. He takes over from Effiom Ekot, who was promoted to Assistant Inspector General of Police and transferred to the Office of the National Security Adviser in Abuja. The Inspector General of Police, Kayode Egbetokun, approved Abdullahi’s posting.

Born in Kano Municipal, Kano State, Abdullahi joined the Nigeria Police Force in 1992 as a Cadet Assistant Superintendent after completing training at the Police Academy Annexe in Kaduna. He later obtained a master’s degree in Public Policy Administration from Bayero University, Kano, in 2005.

Abdullahi’s service record includes various positions such as Patrol and Guard duty, Divisional Crime Officer, Divisional Traffic Officer, and Divisional Police Officer in multiple locations. Prior to his new assignment, he served as Commissioner of Police, Procurement, at Force Headquarters, Abuja.

The Jigawa State Police Command voiced its confidence that Abdullahi’s experience, strategic plans, and collaborative mindset will strengthen security in the region. He is urging full support and cooperation from security agencies, traditional rulers, religious leaders, and other community stakeholders in efforts to share intelligence and jointly tackle crime throughout Jigawa State and its environs.

article_content: The California Science Center is set to launch a significant stage in the building of the Samuel Oschin Air and Space Center by installing Endeavour’s huge solid rocket motors. Weighing 104,000 pounds each and measuring 116 feet long—about as long as a Boeing 757—the motors reached Los Angeles from Mojave Air and Space Port back in October. Previously responsible for more than 80% of Endeavour’s liftoff power, these motors will be installed using two cranes: a smaller one to pivot them upright, and a larger one to lower each onto the aft skirts, the 9-foot-tall bases positioned in July. Science Center President Jeffrey Rudolph called this the first major milestone, as these impressive rockets start stacking up to form the shuttle exhibit. Work kicks off at 8 a.m. Tuesday, with the team moving the rockets from their spot near the dining terraces to the construction area. The museum will provide a livestream for those who’d like to watch. After lifting the first rocket, crews will secure it with roughly 180 robust pins—each one inch in diameter and two inches long. The job could take a few hours or potentially run into the night, depending on how well things align. The second rocket is scheduled for installation no earlier than November 8. After both boosters are mounted, scaffolding will be set up so specialists can attach the nose cones and front skirts, finishing the rockets’ assembly. The next step will be attaching the big orange fuel tank in early January, followed by raising the Endeavour orbiter to its vertical, launch-like position during the last week of January. Some cranes used will be as tall as Los Angeles City Hall. When finished, the $400 million Samuel Oschin Air and Space Center will stand 20 stories high. It will be the only museum in the country to show a shuttle upright, as if ready for launch—a true one-of-a-kind exhibit. NASA selected the Science Center for this honor in 2011, making it one of just three U.S. sites to host a space-flown orbiter. Since arriving in 2012, Endeavour has been on view in a temporary warehouse. It stays there until December 31, after which close visitor access may pause for several years while the new display is assembled.

article_content: The Royal Air Force's Red Arrows display team has been placed under “special measures” following a damning report highlighting extensive predatory behavior toward women. The investigation, which found evidence of a widespread toxic culture, revealed that women on the team were subject to sexual harassment, bullying, and were sometimes treated like “property.” Specific examples included unwanted physical contact, inappropriate sexual messages, and invitations to engage in sexual activity. According to the report, such actions were often overlooked due to a persistent bystander culture. The formal inquiry began in 2021 after three women brought unresolved complaints to the attention of the head of the RAF. The investigation reviewed incidents tracing back to 2017. In response, Defence Minister Andrew Murrison confirmed that leadership changes had taken place and that the Red Arrows squadron, based at RAF Waddington, is now being strictly supervised. At a Commons Defence Select Committee meeting, Murrison emphasized that no defense division is exempt from standards regarding unacceptable conduct. While the term 'special measures' is usually applied to underperforming institutions such as hospitals or schools taken over for close oversight, the Defence Minister did not provide additional specifics. Unlike Murrison’s firm stance, Air Chief Marshal Sir Richard Knighton expressed his shock at the report’s findings but clarified that there are no plans to disband the Red Arrows. The RAF admitted there was a perception among some team members that they were 'special' due to the team's public profile, frequent interaction with VIPs and celebrities, and admiring audiences, which may have contributed to disregard for proper standards. By early 2023, the Red Arrows had completed almost 5,000 shows across 57 countries. Sir Richard Knighton issued an unreserved apology to anyone affected, acknowledging that the reputation of the team had been harmed by a minority of individuals. He pointed out that few of those involved in inappropriate behavior remain on the team. He also highlighted that reforms have been introduced, with a focus on leadership changes, cultural transformation, and strengthened protections to address the systemic issues outlined in the investigation.

استانداردها و رفتارهای نامناسب مصون باشد. اگرچه عبارت «اقدامات ویژه» معمولاً درباره بیمارستان‌ها یا مدارس ناکارآمدی به کار می‌رود که تحت نظارت خارج از سازمان قرار می‌گیرند، وزیر دفاع جزئیات بیشتری article_content: According to a recent Times of India (TOI) report, four out of five families in Mumbai have experienced at least one member suffering from a sore throat or cough. Approximately 85% of these families attribute their health issues to dust caused by construction and roads, while 62% blame vehicular emissions for the city’s poor air quality. A nationwide online survey conducted by LocalCircles found varied health impacts across cities: people in Delhi more commonly experience burning eyes, whereas Mumbai residents report more sore throats. Nearly 7,000 Mumbai residents participated in the survey, with 44% stating they experienced burning eyes due to pollution. While Mumbai’s pollution levels remain lower than those in Delhi, the city has seen a steady increase in poor air quality days over the past five years. Residents are coping with air pollution through different measures, such as using anti-pollution masks, air purifiers at home, and consuming immunity-boosting foods. However, half of Mumbai respondents said they haven’t taken any preventive actions. During a recent World Cup match in Mumbai, PM2.5 levels exceeded the safe limit by over 14 times, which led to a post-match ban on firecrackers due to poor air quality. Many cricketers voiced their concerns about pollution during practice sessions. On Tuesday, the Bombay High Court took suo motu cognizance of air pollution concerns in Mumbai and its suburbs, requesting responses from the BMC, Maharashtra Pollution Control Board (MPCB), and Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) regarding possible mitigation steps. Data from SAFAR (System of Air Quality and Weather Forecasting and Research) show that Mumbai has consistently experienced 'unhealthy' air pollution levels since late September. Authorities are considering measures such as anti-smog guns and sprinkler systems at construction sites to reduce dust. In other news, Apple Inc. reported record quarterly revenue in India during September, with strong year-over-year growth, according to CEO Tim Cook. Luxury carmakers report that younger buyers are driving increased sales in India. Meanwhile, uncertainty surrounds leadership at the proposed Sony-Zee merger as CEO Punit Goenka is under investigation by SEBI.

article_content: Lisa Somerville, a 28-year-old mother from Kirkintilloch near Glasgow, is fortunate to be alive after a serious car crash. While driving home from work in a heavy rainstorm in May 2009, Lisa lost control of her car on a slippery, narrow road and collided head-on with another vehicle. She was not wearing her seatbelt at the time. Lisa sustained serious injuries, including a punctured lung, four cracked ribs, and a broken nose, and had to be freed from the wreckage by firefighters. She was rushed to the Royal Infirmary for emergency care. After regaining consciousness, doctors informed her that the padded inserts—often called 'chicken fillets'—in her bra absorbed some of the impact and may have prevented her cracked ribs from penetrating her heart, potentially saving her life. Lisa, who has worn bra inserts for years due to insecurities about her chest size, admits that she was doubling up on the inserts that day, wearing two per side. While she had always disliked wearing them and felt uncomfortable about her body, she was grateful for the protection they offered during the accident. Following the crash, the unexpected attention on her body left her feeling more self-conscious and unhappy. Eventually, she decided to undergo cosmetic surgery, paying £4,000 for breast augmentation, which increased her size from AAA to 30E. Lisa now says she feels more confident and happier, though she remains grateful to the 'chicken fillets' that protected her in the crash.

article_content: A telecommunications cable connecting Sweden and Estonia in the Baltic Sea was damaged earlier this month, around the same time as a Finnish-Estonian pipeline and cable, according to Sweden's civil defence minister. Despite the damage, the cable remains operational. Finnish investigators have identified vessels in the area at the time of the pipeline and cable damage on October 8, including a Russian-flagged ship and a Chinese-owned vessel. The Russian authority for nuclear-powered vessels, Atomflot, denied that one of its ships was involved. The Swedish-Estonian cable was damaged outside Sweden’s territorial waters and exclusive economic zone, civil defence minister Carl-Oskar Bohlin said, but it continues to function. 'We can't say at the moment what caused this damage,' he told reporters, noting the incident occurred at a similar time and location to the damage reported to a gas pipeline and telecom cable between Estonia and Finland. Network provider Arelion confirmed that one of its subsea fibre cables was 'partially damaged.' A spokesperson said the cause is unknown and repairs are planned in the coming weeks, depending on weather conditions. According to Estonia’s Economic Affairs and Communications Ministry, the damage occurred on a cable to Sweden approximately 50km west of Hiiumaa Island. A NATO official told Reuters that the alliance is aware of the reported damage to the Swedish-Estonian cable, remains in close contact with both countries, and is monitoring the situation. Estonia is a NATO member, while Sweden's membership is awaiting ratification. Rear Admiral Ewa Skoog Haslum, head of Sweden’s navy, said maintaining security over surface and undersea traffic in the Baltic is challenging due to heavy activity, noting, 'The situation at sea is very intense.' Recent incidents have increased European and NATO concerns over the vulnerability of vital infrastructure in and under the Baltic Sea, following the September 2022 explosions that ruptured the Nord Stream pipelines. On October 8, Finland said the Balticconnector subsea gas pipeline and a telecom cable linking Finland and Estonia had been damaged possibly by a deliberate act. Finnish authorities reported external marks on the seabed near the damaged pipeline and are reviewing vessel traffic in the area. Finland's National Bureau of Investigation used open sources to identify several vessels, including the NewNew Polar Bear (operated by a Chinese company) and Sevmorput (a Russian-flagged nuclear-powered cargo ship), which were present in the area at the relevant time. Their backgrounds and past activities are being examined in cooperation with international authorities. Atomflot, owner of Sevmorput and part of the Russian nuclear company Rosatom, rejected suggestions their vessel was involved, stating that Sevmorput transited the Gulf of Finland without incident. NewNew Shipping, owner of the NewNew Polar Bear, declined to comment. Sweden’s Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson highlighted the complexity of protecting the 'spaghetti' of pipes and cables under the Baltic and said Sweden and its Joint Expeditionary Force partners would seek ways to improve infrastructure protection.

مسئول کشتی‌های هسته‌ای، اتم‌فلوت، هرگونه دخالت یکی از کشتی‌های خود را رد کرده است. این کابل سوئدی-استونیایی خارج از آب‌های سرزمینی و منطقه انحصاری اقتصادی سوئد آسیب دیده اما به کار خود ادامه می‌دهد؛ لوله گاز و کابل مخابراتی بین استونی و فنلاند رخ داده است. ارائه‌دهنده شبکه، آرلیون، تأیید کرد که یکی از کابل‌های فیبر زیردریایی‌اش «به طور جزئی آسیب دیده». سخنگوی شرکت گفت علت آسیب مشخص نیست و تعمیر کابل در هفته‌های آینده با توجه به شرایط آب و هوایی انجام خواهد شد. بر اساس اعلام وزارت اقتصاد و ارتباطات استونی، این آسیب به کابلی به سمت سوئد، حدود ۵۰ کیلومتری غرب جزیره هییوما وارد شده است. یک مقام ناتو به رویترز گفت که این اتحادیه از گزارش آسیب به کابل سوئد-استونی مطلع است، با هر دو کشور در تماس نزدیک بوده و وضعیت را زیر نظر دارد. استونی عضو ناتو است و عضویت سوئد در حال تصویب است. دریابد اوا اسکوگ هاسلوم، رئیس نیروی دریایی سوئد گفت تأمین امنیت تردد سطحی و زیرسطحی در دریای بالتیک به دلیل تراکم رفت‌وآمد چالش‌برانگیز است و افزود: «اوضاع در دریا بسیار پُر تنش است». اتفاق‌های اخیر نگرانی اروپا و ناتو را نسبت به آسیب‌پذیری زیرساخت‌های حیاتی در سطح و زیر دریای بالتیک افزایش داده است؛ به‌ویژه پس از انفجارهای سپتامبر ۲۰۲۲ که باعث انفجار خطوط لوله نورد استریم شد. در ۸ اکتبر، فنلاند اعلام کرد که خط لوله گاز زیردریایی بالتیک‌کانکتور و یک کابل مخابراتی بین فنلاند و استونی احتمالاً به عمد آسیب دیده‌اند. مسئولان فنلاندی آثار خارجی روی بستر دریا در نزدیک محل آسیب را کشف کرده‌اند و هم‌اکنون ترافیک کشتی‌ها را در آن منطقه بررسی می‌کنند. اداره ملی تحقیقات فنلاند با استفاده از منابع باز چند کشتی، از جمله نیو نیو پولار بر (متعلق به یک شرکت چینی) و سویمورپوت (کشتی باری هسته‌ای با پرچم روسیه) را شناسایی کرده که در زمان حادثه در محل حضور داشته‌اند. سوابق و فعالیت‌های قبلی این کشتی‌ها با همکاری مقامات کشورهای دیگر بررسی می‌شود. اتم‌فلوت، مالک سویمورپوت و زیرمجموعه شرکت هسته‌ای روس‌اتم، هرگونه دخالت این کشتی را رد کرده و اعلام کرد سویمورپوت بدون توقف از خلیج فنلاند عبور کرده است. شرکت نیو نیو شیپینگ، مالک نیو نیو پولار بر، از اظهار نظر خودداری کرد. اولف کریسترسون، نخست‌وزیر سوئد، به پیچیدگی حفاظت از «رشته» خطوط لوله و کابل‌های زیردریایی در بستر دریای بالتیک اشاره کرد و گفت سوئد و شرکایش در نیروی اعزامی مشترک به دنبال راه‌هایی برای تقویت حفاظت از زیرساخت‌های حیاتی هستند.

article_content: On Thursday, President Bola Tinubu signed into law the Defence Industries Corporation of Nigeria (DICON) Bill, 2023. This new Act repeals the previous version of the DICON Act, according to a statement released by Ajuri Ngelale, the President’s Special Adviser on Media and Publicity. DICON was initially established by an act of parliament on August 1, 1964, and was later updated in Chapter 94 of Nigeria’s federal laws in 2004. The newly enacted Bill, sponsored by Babajimi Benson, Chairman of the House of Representatives Defence Committee (APC – Ikorodu), expands DICON’s authority to oversee subsidiaries and operate ordnance factories that are responsible for manufacturing, storing, and disposing of military equipment and related material. A major advancement in this legislation is the creation of the Defence Industry Technology, Research, and Development Institute, aimed at promoting Nigeria’s military technological base through multidisciplinary research across military institutes, commercialization, and strengthening of the country’s defence capabilities. The Act also introduces extensive regulations for how defence materials are produced, stored, distributed, and disposed of, and it seeks to attract private investment into the sector by ensuring transparent and reliable processes for research and production.

article_content: Dyson, founded by Sir James Dyson in 1993, has announced a £250 million expansion plan marking its biggest period of growth to date. This project will create 3,000 new jobs in science and engineering, signaling major investment in Britain’s manufacturing sector and reflecting renewed economic optimism in the UK. Dyson is currently applying for planning permission to build a large new laboratory and campus—with its own sports pitch—next to its headquarters in Malmesbury, Wiltshire. If the application is approved, the facility could open in 2016 and employ around 1,000 engineers and scientists working on advanced projects like domestic robots and robotic vacuum cleaners. The company then plans to build two more laboratories, adding 2,000 more staff. After launching the world’s first bagless vacuum cleaner, the DC01, in 1993, Dyson has grown into a leading British manufacturing success, having produced its 50 millionth machine last year. Adding to the upbeat news for the UK economy, KFC has revealed plans to open 150 new restaurants in the UK and Ireland over the next five years, creating 6,000 jobs.

article_content: Filmmaker Karan Johar has recently expressed regret for aspects of his past work, admitting in interviews that he often misunderstood gender politics in his films, especially in 'Kuch Kuch Hota Hai'. He recognized that the main character displayed signs of toxicity. Johar has attempted to address these shortcomings with his latest film, 'Rocky Aur Rani Kii Prem Kahaani', an imperfect yet sincere movie that thoughtfully tackles social issues. However, he has not apologized for 'Dostana', which was once considered a milestone for Hindi cinema when it released in 2008 but now seems outdated. 'Dostana' is an unofficial remake of the Adam Sandler comedy, 'I Now Pronounce You Chuck and Larry', and follows two straight men, Sameer (Abhishek Bachchan) and Kunal (John Abraham), who pretend to be gay to secure residency in the US. They move in with Neha (Priyanka Chopra), posing as a couple, while both develop feelings for her. The story unfolds with comedic misunderstandings, but its climax and treatment of LGBTQIA+ themes are now viewed as insensitive. Directed by Tarun Mansukhani, 'Dostana' is marking its 15th anniversary. On rewatch, its outdated approach stands out, especially when compared to 'Milk', the acclaimed film about gay rights activist Harvey Milk, released the same year. While celebrated at the time, 'Dostana's lack of serious engagement with LGBTQIA+ discrimination and use of stereotypes has drawn criticism. The film features no genuine queer characters, aside from a caricature portrayed by Boman Irani. The narrative centers on privileged protagonists who exploit LGBTQIA+ identities for personal gain, with little reflection on the realities faced by the community. Neha is depicted as naive, and several plot points involve her and others being manipulated by Sameer and Kunal. In the film's conclusion, the two men must kiss to prove their apology, a moment handled with discomfort and played for laughs. Despite previous plans for a sequel, Karan Johar did not move forward, with Kartik Aaryan withdrawing from the project. translated_content: کارگردان فیلم، کارن جوهر، اخیراً بابت بخش‌هایی از آثار گذشته‌اش ابراز پشیمانی کرده و در مصاحبه‌هایی اعتراف کرده است که اغلب سیاست‌های جنسیتی را در فیلم‌هایش به خوبی درک نکرده، به ویژه در فیلم «کچ کچ هوتا هی». او پذیرفته است که شخصیت اصلی فیلم نشانه‌هایی از رفتارهای منفی داشته است. جوهر سعی کرده این کمبودها را با فیلم جدیدش «راکی اور رانی کی پریم کهانی» جبران کند؛ این فیلم هرچند بی‌نقص نیست اما با صداقت به مسائل اجتماعی می‌پردازد. با این وجود، او تاکنون بابت فیلم «دوستانه» که زمانی نقطه عطفی در سینمای هند بود و در سال ۲۰۰۸ اکران شد اما اکنون کهنه به نظر می‌رسد، عذرخواهی نکرده است. «دوستانه» بازسازی غیررسمی کمدی «من حالا شما را چاک و لری اعلام می‌کنم» با بازی آدام سندلر است و داستان دو مرد دگرجنس‌گرا به نام‌های سمیر (آبیشک باچان) و کونال (جان آبراهام) را روایت می‌کند که برای گرفتن اقامت آمریکا وانمود می‌کنند همجنس‌گرا هستند. آن‌ها با نِها (پریانکا چوپرا) همخانه می‌شوند و تظاهر می‌کنند زوج هستند، در حالی که هر دو به او علاقه‌مند می‌شوند. داستان با سوءتفاهم‌های کمدی پیش می‌رود، اما اوج داستان و پرداخت مضمون LGBTQIA+ اکنون ناپخته و نامناسب تلقی می‌شود. این فیلم به کارگردانی تارون منسخانی اکنون پانزدهمین سالگرد اکرانش را جشن می‌گیرد. بازبینی دوباره فیلم، ضعف‌های دیدگاهی آن را برجسته می‌کند، به ویژه نسبت به فیلم موفق «میلک» درباره هاروی میلک، فعال حقوق همجنس‌گرایان که همان سال اکران شد. اگرچه «دوستانه» آن زمان تحسین شد، اما بی‌توجهی‌اش به تبعیض واقعی و استفاده از کلیشه‌های جامعه LGBTQIA+ مورد انتقاد قرار گرفته است. فیلم حتی یک شخصیت واقعی از این جامعه ندارد جز یک کاریکاتور با بازی بومن ایرانی. روایت، روی شخصیت‌هایی تمرکز دارد که هویت جامعه LGBTQIA+ را برای منافع خود سوءاستفاده می‌کنند و چندان به واقعیت‌های آن جامعه نمی‌پردازد. نِها شخصیتی ساده‌لوح دارد و در طول فیلم چند بار او و دیگران توسط سمیر و کونال فریب می‌خورند. در پایان، این دو مرد برای اثبات عذرخواهی خود باید همدیگر را ببوسند؛ صحنه‌ای که با شوخی و ناراحتی نمایش داده می‌شود. اگرچه قبلاً برنامه‌هایی برای ساخت دنباله وجود داشت اما کارن جوهر آن را ادامه نداد و کارتیک آریان نیز از پروژه کنار کشید. ستون «پست کرِدیت سین» به بررسی انتقادی فیلم‌های جدید از نظر محتوا، کیفیت ساخت و شخصیت‌پردازی می‌پردازد. برای اخبار بروزشده و جدیدترین اخبار بالیوود، ایندین اکسپرس را دنبال کنید.

article_content: Russia has failed to be re-elected as a member of the United Nations Human Rights Council. The country was suspended from the top human rights body in April 2022, following its invasion of Ukraine. Russia had hoped to secure a new three-year term, which it believed would reveal divisions among UN member states over support for Ukraine. However, Bulgaria and Albania secured the two seats allocated to Eastern European countries instead. The voting took place shortly after a Russian missile strike killed 52 people in the north-eastern Ukrainian village of Hroza. In the vote, Russia received 83 votes from the 193 UN General Assembly members, compared with 160 for Bulgaria and 123 for Albania. Earlier, Albania's ambassador Ferit Hoxha stated it was important for member states to show they were not willing to 'take an arsonist for a firefighter.' Russia pledged to find 'adequate solutions for human rights issues' and expressed concerns about the council becoming an 'instrument which serves political wills of one group of countries,' a phrase understood to refer to Western nations. Diplomats said Russia was seeking to restore international credibility after being accused of widespread human rights violations both in Ukraine and within its own borders. Russia claimed it would attract votes from many countries, particularly developing nations, in the secret ballot—suggesting that some privately supported Moscow but chose not to do so publicly so as not to anger Western countries. Reports indicate that Russia campaigned actively, allegedly offering small countries grain and weapons in exchange for votes. Russia's ambassador to the UN, Vassily Nebenzia, accused the United States of leading a campaign to block Russia’s return to the council. Russia was suspended from the Human Rights Council in April 2022 with 93 UN General Assembly members voting in favor, 24 against, and 58 abstaining. From 2024, the council will include: Albania, Brazil, Bulgaria, Burundi, China, Ivory Coast, Cuba, Dominican Republic, France, Ghana, Indonesia, Japan, Kuwait, Malawi, and the Netherlands. These countries will serve three-year terms.
translated_content: روسیه نتوانست دوباره به عنوان عضو شورای حقوق بشر سازمان ملل انتخاب شود. این کشور در آوریل ۲۰۲۲، پس از حمله به اوکراین، از این نهاد مهم حقوق بشری تعلیق شد. روسیه امیدوار بود که با کسب یک دوره سه ساله جدید، اختلاف نظر میان کشورهای عضو سازمان ملل بر سر حمایت از اوکراین آشکار شود. با این حال، بلغارستان و آلبانی دو کرسی ویژه کشورهای اروپای شرقی را از آن خود کردند. رای‌گیری اندکی پس از حمله موشکی روسیه که جان ۵۲ نفر را در روستای هروزا در شمال‌شرق اوکراین گرفت، برگزار شد. در این رای‌گیری، روسیه ۸۳ رأی از مجموع ۱۹۳ عضو مجمع عمومی سازمان ملل دریافت کرد، در حالی که بلغارستان ۱۶۰ و آلبانی ۱۲۳ رأی کسب کردند. پیش‌تر، فریت هوخا، سفیر آلبانی، اعلام کرده بود مهم است کشورهای عضو نشان دهند 'آتش‌افروز را جای آتش‌نشان نمی‌پذیرند.' روسیه وعده داد 'راه‌حل‌های مناسب برای مسائل حقوق بشر' پیدا کند و نسبت به تبدیل شورا به 'ابزاری در خدمت خواسته‌های سیاسی یک گروه از کشورها'—که منظور غرب است—ابراز نگرانی کرد. دیپلمات‌ها می‌گویند روسیه پس از متهم شدن به نقض گسترده حقوق بشر در اوکراین و داخل کشور، در تلاش برای بازگرداندن اعتبار بین‌المللی خود بوده است. روسیه مدعی بود در رای‌گیری مخفی، به ویژه آرای کشورهای در حال توسعه را به دست می‌آورد، اما برخی کشورها برای جلوگیری از خشم غرب علناً از مسکو حمایت نمی‌کنند. گزارش‌ها حاکی است روسیه به طور فعال کمپین کرده و ظاهراً به کشورهای کوچک در برابر رای‌شان غلات و سلاح پیشنهاد داده است. واسیلی نبنزیا، سفیر روسیه در سازمان ملل، ایالات متحده را متهم به رهبری کارزاری برای جلوگیری از بازگشت روسیه به شورا کرد. روسیه در آوریل ۲۰۲۲ با ۹۳ رأی موافق، ۲۴ رأی مخالف و ۵۸ رأی ممتنع از شورای حقوق بشر تعلیق شد. از سال ۲۰۲۴، اعضای شورای حقوق بشر شامل آلبانی، برزیل، بلغارستان، بوروندی، چین، ساحل عاج، کوبا، جمهوری دومینیکن، فرانسه، غنا، اندونزی، ژاپن، کویت، مالاوی و هلند هستند و به مدت سه سال در شورا حضور خواهند داشت.

Along the French Mediterranean coast near Spain, warm autumn days bring tourists, but local residents face disruption: France closed four minor border roads to its southern neighbor two years ago. The government cited growing illegal migration and anti-terrorism needs, but residents of Banyuls-sur-Mer, a town of 6,000, say the closures have cut vital economic, cultural, and family links long shared across the border.

The closure of the Col de Banyuls, a historic escape route during past conflicts, has become especially symbolic. Protests led by the 'Alberes without borders' group and organized by retired lawyer Pierre Becque, highlight decades of cross-border ties—even noting the physical movement of border rocks to allow passage for bikes and pedestrians. Authorities argue focusing policing on main crossings is more efficient, especially given an 82% rise in illegal migration reported in 2022, and maintain that roads may reopen if joint police units are established. Recent terror attacks keep security a top priority.

Meanwhile, local officials and business owners argue the closures have damaged the key wine industry, as seasonal Spanish workers now face difficult journeys. Grapes have gone unharvested, and the economic pain is felt on both sides. In Espolla, Spain, a boulder from the border is now a monument to the continued protests. Local councillor Josep Maria Tegido and others maintain these closures harm historic cross-border life, and push for renewed cooperation to restore connections that have lasted centuries.

در امتداد ساحل مدیترانه فرانسه، نزدیک به مرز اسپانیا، اگرچه روزهای گرم پاییزی گردشگران را جذب می‌کند، اما ساکنان محلی با چالش‌هایی روبرو هستند: فرانسه دو سال پیش چهار جاده فرعی مرزی به اسپانیا را بست. دولت دلیل این اقدام را افزایش مهاجرت غیرقانونی و نیاز به مقابله با تروریسم اعلام کرده است، اما مردم بانیول-سور-مر با جمعیتی حدود ۶۰۰۰ نفر می‌گویند بسته شدن جاده‌ها، پیوندهای اقتصادی، فرهنگی و خانوادگی دیرین با اسپانیا را قطع کرده است.

بسته شدن کول دو بانیول، مسیری تاریخی و نمادین که در گذشته راه فرار در دوران بحران‌ها بوده، تأثیر زیادی داشته است. حرکت اعتراضی گروه «آلبِر بدون مرز» با رهبری وکیل بازنشسته پیر بک، دهه‌ها روابط دوسویه مرزی را یادآوری می‌کند—حتی اشاره می‌شود که برخی سنگ‌های مرزی برای عبور عابران و دوچرخه‌سواران جابجا شده‌اند. مسئولان دولتی بر تمرکز پلیس روی گذرگاه‌های اصلی تأکید دارند، به‌ویژه با افزایش ۸۲ درصدی مهاجرت غیرقانونی در سال ۲۰۲۲، و مطرح کرده‌اند شاید با استقرار تیم‌های مشترک پلیس جاده‌ها دوباره باز شود. رخدادهای تروریستی اخیر اولویت امنیتی را بالا برده است.

در همین حال، مدیران محلی و فعالان اقتصادی معتقدند این بسته شدن به صنعت عمده شراب منطقه لطمه زده و دسترسی کارگران فصلی اسپانیایی را بسیار دشوار کرده است. بسیاری از انگورها برداشت نشدند و آثار منفی اقتصادی در هر دو سوی مرز احساس می‌شود. در اسپویای اسپانیا، یک سنگ مرزی به نمادی برای اعتراض تبدیل شده است. خوزه ماریا تجیدو، کشاورز و عضو شورای محلی، و دیگران تأکید دارند این محدودیت‌ها به جریان تاریخی زندگی مرزی آسیب می‌زند و خواستار احیای همکاری‌های دیرینه هستند.

Radamel Falcao continues to attract interest from English clubs, including Liverpool, despite his desire to join Real Madrid. The Colombian striker, who transferred to Monaco from Atletico Madrid for £50 million last year, is reportedly unhappy in the French league and eager to return to Madrid. Real Madrid, after spending £90 million this summer on James Rodriguez, Toni Kroos, and Keylor Navas, is limited by UEFA’s Financial Fair Play regulations and must now curb further spending.

While Real Madrid would prefer to take Falcao on loan with an option to purchase him next season, Monaco insists any deal should involve an immediate purchase rather than a loan. Nevertheless, Monaco is open to loaning Falcao to another club if Real Madrid does not make a formal bid before the transfer window closes in two weeks. In that case, Falcao may consider a one-year loan elsewhere, hoping for a move to Real Madrid next summer.

Liverpool manager Brendan Rodgers has prioritized signing another striker before the window closes and is a known admirer of Falcao. While Liverpool acknowledges that Falcao is likely to favor a move to Madrid, the club plans to keep an eye on the situation and may try to persuade him if the Real move does not materialize. Despite Falcao’s £200,000-a-week wage demands, Liverpool does not foresee financial issues with a potential deal. Monaco is asking for a £12 million loan fee, although that amount is negotiable.

Manchester City has also expressed interest in Falcao but has not pursued negotiations further at this time. Additionally, Liverpool is monitoring Fiorentina goalkeeper Norberto Neto as a possible addition before the end of the month. With Pepe Reina having joined Bayern Munich, Liverpool seeks to add depth and competition for their current No.1, Simon Mignolet, with Brad Jones serving as backup. Liverpool’s search for a new striker is in part to fill the vacancy left by Luis Suarez’s departure.
